raw.assessment: The incumbent demonstrably preserves design selection and detects some fit errors before dispatch. Reopening seams plausibly contributes to the 37-minute median, but its contribution is unmeasured. Rework affected five of eight large covers, two of fourteen medium covers, and no small covers; this supports investigating size-dependent allowances without establishing their cause. Unadjusted small covers taking 25–31 minutes show that some existing work meets the time target. The concrete limiting observation is that both observed customer first-placement failures involved rounded corners absent from the reference tables: passing the existing check may therefore miss customer geometry. Shrinkage, operator effects, and actual dimensions remain unresolved; estimated waste by weight does not establish the area limit.

openings.claim: A common cutting allowance may create a systematic fit discrepancy that increases with table size; cutting the entire batch first could propagate that discrepancy before feedback arrives.
openings.delta: Use early completed ordered covers to distinguish a repeatable size-related discrepancy from variation in execution before committing the remaining cuts.
openings.prediction: If allowance is responsible, measured finished dimensions will deviate consistently from the intended fit for a given size despite accurate cutting and seam execution. If discrepancies instead track worker or cloth direction, a size-only correction should fail to explain them.
openings.probe: Sequence one ordered cover of each size through cutting, sewing, and fitting. Record cutting dimensions, seam uptake, finished dimensions, cloth direction, worker, and stage times. Correct subsequent cutting cards only if measurements support it; account for pilot labor and projected cutting waste by area within the existing batch.
assumptions: The observed size association may be confounded by design, direction, or worker.
Pilot sequencing must fit the three-week window and 350-unit limit.

openings.claim: Do rounded corners predict installation problems after actual tabletop dimensions and finished cover dimensions are accounted for?
openings.delta: Separate missing corner geometry from incorrect nominal dimensions as the reason the reference-table check misses customer failures.
openings.prediction: A corner-geometry explanation predicts localized pocket slack or tension on rounded tables with otherwise matching dimensions. A nominal-dimension explanation predicts dimensional mismatch sufficient to explain failure regardless of corner shape.
openings.probe: Obtain actual length, width, and corner measurements from the six willing customers, prioritizing the four nominal-only orders where accessible. Compare these with order and finished-cover dimensions and record the location of fit problems during first placement. Use findings to identify which reference checks require supplementary customer geometry checks.
assumptions: Willing customers may not include the nominal-only orders or enough corner variation to distinguish explanations.
Any later pocket modification still requires the stipulated wash and tool-free removal checks.

raw.assessment: The observations suggest two fitting problems worth separating: larger-size construction errors and differences between customer and reference-table geometry. Neither cause is established. Any trial must honor size and design, use existing stock and machines, pass the five-cycle wash test, stay within 350 currency units and three weeks, and verify cutting waste by area at no more than 8%. Success remains at least 38 of 40 first placements, all ordered designs, and median cooperative time at most 32 minutes, including trial and adjustment work.

openings.claim: A size-dependent error in the common cutting allowance may contribute to larger-cover rework; verified size-specific cards and staged cutting could prevent that error propagating through the batch.
openings.delta: Sew and measure initial covers before releasing the remaining cuts, allowing supported allowance corrections while stock is still uncut.
openings.prediction: If the allowance is responsible, measured cut-to-finished dimensional errors should recur with a consistent sign within a size before washing. Errors appearing mainly after washing or changing with cloth direction would weaken that explanation.
openings.probe: Start with one ordered cover per size; record card dimensions, actual cuts, finished dimensions, fitting error, design, direction and operator. Repeat a problematic size before revising its card. Measure retained offcuts in both axes through the stipulated wash cycles. Hold further cuts until the proposed correction fits the area-waste budget; record work minutes and subsequent rework.
assumptions: Staged cutting fits the delivery window.
An allowance correction can be accommodated by remaining stock without excess waste.
Initial differences require replication because size, design and operator may be confounded.

openings.claim: Corner-pocket geometry may explain some installation failures independently of nominal tabletop length and width; matching pockets to measured corner shape could improve first placement.
openings.delta: Treat corner shape as an order-specific fitting input alongside the selected table size.
openings.prediction: Among tables with matching measured length and width, installation difficulty should track corner shape; a corner-matched pocket should remove that difficulty without changing the ordered size or design.
openings.probe: Request actual dimensions and corner measurements from the six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders where available. Compare square and rounded corner fits using retained-offcut pocket trials. Verify a supported construction on an ordered cover at its specified table, including removal and the same five-cycle wash test, before wider adoption.
assumptions: Willing customers include useful geometry contrasts.
Corner changes retain the ordered visible design and fit existing stock layouts.
Measurement and sewing time remain compatible with the batch target.

openings.claim: Common allowances may cause size-related errors; staged cutting could prevent propagation.
openings.discriminator: Repeatable signed prewash errors within size despite accurate execution support allowance error; worker, design, direction or postwash patterns suggest alternatives.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints conditionally; correction must fit remaining stock and area-waste budget.
openings.probe: Complete one ordered cover per size before further cuts; record card/actual cuts, seam uptake, finished dimensions, fit, design, direction, worker and stage times. Repeat a problematic size before revising cards. Wash retained offcuts through five cycles, measuring both axes; track subsequent rework.
openings.uncertainty: Size associations are confounded; rework's time contribution and width shrinkage are unknown. Pilot sequencing and corrections may strain time or stock.

openings.claim: Customer corner shape may independently defeat reference-table fit; measured geometry could guide supplementary checks and matched pockets.
openings.discriminator: With actual table and cover dimensions accounted for, localized slack/tension tracking corner shape supports geometry; dimensional mismatch sufficient regardless of shape supports nominal-dimension error.
openings.fit: Conditional on ordered size/design, stock layouts, wash durability and tool-free removal.
openings.probe: Obtain actual length, width and corners from six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders where accessible. Locate first-placement failures; compare square/rounded fits with offcut pocket trials. Verify supported pockets on an ordered cover at its specified table, including removal and five-cycle washing, before expansion.
openings.uncertainty: Customers may lack nominal-only orders or useful geometry contrasts; measurement/sewing costs remain unmeasured.

post_distill.decision: Probe both; neither cause is established. Preserve ordered selections, purchased stock, two machines, five-cycle durability and tool-free removal; stay within 350 units and three weeks. Verify waste by area <=8% (weight estimate insufficient). Count trial/adjustment labor: require >=38/40 first placements, all designs correct, median <=32 minutes.
